archetypes.name: shard-wiring
archetypes.rationale: The plan asserts no new Makefile target or shard registration is needed for test-trailer-awk.sh, but this rests on the assumption that invoke-only thin adapters already pass the shard-coverage check; that assumption needs verification against actual Makefile targets and shard entries.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the plan's claim that test-trailer-awk.sh needs no new Makefile target or shard entry is correct. Read the Makefile and any shard-coverage scripts (e.g. the target responsible for make test-harness-shards-coverage or equivalent) to find how test-*.sh files in skills/design/scripts/ are discovered and registered. Check whether existing invoke-only thin adapters (test-trailer-dedup.sh, test-trailer-has-any.sh, test-trailer-validate.sh) are absent from Makefile targets and shard entries, confirming the precedent the plan cites. If the shard check enumerates all test-*.sh files in the directory, adding test-trailer-awk.sh without registration would break CI even though behavior is correct — flag this as a plan gap if the precedent does not hold. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: line-anchor
archetypes.rationale: The plan cites specific line numbers in test-design-structure.sh (397-402, 403, 407, 404-405, 409-410, 412-415) and instructs edits only at those exact lines; if those line numbers have shifted in HEAD the targeted edits will corrupt or miss the intended anchors.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/test-design-structure.sh and cross-check every specific line number the plan cites: lines 397-402 for SKILL_MD Gate A/B snapshot-trailers/dedup pins, line 403 for the weak snapshot grep on APPROVAL_MD to replace, line 407 for the weak snapshot grep on DISCUSSION_MD to remove, lines 404-405 for diff_added preservation greps to leave untouched, and lines 409-410 and 412-415 for diff_deleted/mechanical_churn preservation greps to leave untouched. Also verify that the contains() helper the plan references at lines 23-25 as an alternative to raw grep actually exists at that location and has the expected signature. Flag any mismatches between the plan's stated line numbers and the actual file content, since stale anchors would cause the implementer to edit wrong lines or skip intended ones. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: md-sibling-convention
archetypes.rationale: The plan creates six new .md sibling files citing parse-plan-commands.md as the structural precedent; the proposed content descriptions must match the exact sections and conventions that pattern and any script-md-siblings lint enforce.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read an existing representative sibling .md file near the trailer scripts (e.g. a test-*.md or lib-*.md in skills/design/scripts/) to understand the exact structure the script-md-siblings convention requires — section headings, invocation examples, caller lists, and edit-in-sync pointer phrasing. Then evaluate whether the plan's descriptions of lib-plan-optional-trailers.md, test-trailer-awk.md, and the four stub files (test-trailer-helpers.md, test-trailer-dedup.md, test-trailer-has-any.md, test-trailer-validate.md) align with that pattern. Flag any described content that departs from the established structure — missing required sections, absent edit-in-sync pointers, or wrong heading levels — since these would fail a script-md-siblings lint that checks structure beyond mere file existence. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
